title: Financial Analyst
description:
Is the opportunity to join a culture where “We Do the Right Thing,” and “We Courageously Shape Our Future Together” important to you? If so, Guardian is seeking a motivated individual to join our team as a Financial Analyst.

Reporting to the Head of Planning & Expense Consolidation, this role plays a central position within Group FP&A, supporting consolidated expense planning, reporting, and strategic analytics across the Group Benefits organization.

The Financial Analyst partners closely with Expense Management, Product, Pricing, and senior leadership to deliver actionable insights, enhance expense transparency, and support business decision-making. This role combines executive reporting, operational rigor, and forward-looking analytics to influence financial outcomes.

**You will**

Expense Planning & Leadership Support

* Own consolidated expense exhibits supporting the annual planning process and executive leadership reviews
* Develop clear, executive-ready materials highlighting key drivers, risks, and opportunities
* Partner with Expense Management to validate planning assumptions

Strategic Expense Analytics

* Support enterprise-wide expense studies and benchmarking initiatives
* Provide detailed analytics across product, department, and account dimensions
* Translate complex financial data into actionable insights
* Strategically partner and support transformational initiatives inclusive of business case development

Unit Cost & Performance Metrics

* Own monthly unit cost reporting, validation, and distribution
* Ensure timely and accurate refresh of YTD expense data
* Enhance visibility into cost efficiency and performance trends

Product Allocations

* Own and maintain product allocation methodologies across Group cost centers
* Partner with Pricing and business leaders to support product margin targets
* Resolve allocation variances across Group and Corporate structures

Transformation & Organizational Support

* Support transformation initiatives and organizational changes
* Validate department alignment and assess financial implications
* Identify opportunities to streamline and improve planning processes

Product Strategy Support

* Partner with product teams on profitability and cost analysis
* Provide expense insights tied to allocations and unit cost drivers

Ad Hoc & Cross-Functional Analysis

* Deliver targeted expense analyses for actuarial, regulatory, and leadership needs
* Support cost management, acquisition, and renewal analysis
* Respond to evolving business priorities with strong analytical support

Systems & Controls

* Participate in UAT testing and enhancements for financial systems (e.g., Oracle)
* Ensure integrity, accuracy, and efficiency of expense reporting processes
* Support automation and modernization of FP&A workflows

Technical Skills

* Excel (advanced beginner to intermediate)
* Formulas (SUMIFS, INDEX/MATCH, basic modeling)
* Data manipulation (pivot tables, lookups)
* Familiarity with financial ledger and planning tools.

Ability to:

* Analyze variances (actual vs plan, forecast vs prior)
* Identify key drivers of financial performance
* Translate data into insights

**You have**

Required

* Bachelor’s degree in Finance, Accounting, Economics, or related field
* 4+ years of FP&A, financial analysis, or expense management experience
* Strong analytical and financial modeling skills
* Advanced Excel and PowerPoint proficiency
* Ability to synthesize complex data into clear, executive-level insights
* Strong communication and collaboration skills

Preferred

* Experience in insurance or financial services
* Familiarity with Oracle Planning / Hyperion / SmartView
* Experience with large, matrixed organizations

**Location/Travel**

Hybrid: 3 days in a Guardian office located in Hudson Yards, NYC; Holmdel NJ; Boston, MA or Bethlehem, PA

$82,770.00 - $135,975.00

The salary range reflected above is a good faith estimate of base pay for the primary location of the position. The salary for this position ultimately will be determined based on the education, experience, knowledge, and abilities of the successful candidate. In addition to salary, this role may also be eligible for annual, sales, or other incentive compensation.

title: FP&A Analyst - Car Rental Business
description:
**Driven to be the Best**

**People. Performance. Purpose.**

At Avis Budget Group, we’re driven to be the best vehicle rental company in the world, together. Our 25,000 employees raise the bar every day, bringing different perspectives, taking ownership, and leading with integrity. We’re defining the future of mobility with safe, sustainable solutions that move people, businesses, and communities forward.

We're looking for an **FP&A Analyst** to join the team supporting financial reporting and performance analysis across our rental business segments. This role sits at the intersection of Sales and Finance — translating commercial performance into financial results and helping the business understand why the numbers move the way they do. The core focus of this role is supporting the ongoing development of our profit allocation tool.

**What You'll Do:**

  

* Prepare recurring and ad hoc reporting on business segment performance (e.g., corporate accounts, channels, geographies, rate/mix)
* Analyze P&L results against sales plans, forecast, and prior year; identify and explain key drivers of variance
* Support the Sales–Finance link by translating account/segment performance trends into financial terms sales leaders can act on, and vice versa
* Assist in building out and maintaining the revenue and cost allocation tool — including logic for attributing P&L cost lines down to the rental agreement level, and applying driver-based allocation methods for costs that can't be directly attributed
* Partner with IT, Risk, and other Finance teams to gather requirements, test logic, and validate outputs as the allocation tool evolves
* Pull and manipulate data from internal systems (Oracle/OCI, Redshift, etc.) using SQL; build and maintain models/reporting in Excel
* Support month-end closing and reporting cycles with accurate, timely deliverables
* Step in to support the wider Commercial Finance team on ad hoc projects and priority requests
* Continuously looking for ways to improve reporting efficiency and data quality

**Perks You’ll Get:**

  

* Access to Medical, Dental, Vision, Life and Disability insurance
* Eligible to elect other voluntary benefits including: Group Auto Insurance, Group Home Insurance, Pet Insurance, Legal Assistance, Identity Theft Protection, FSA, Accident Insurance, Critical Illness Insurance, and additional life insurance coverages
* 401(k) Retirement Plan with company matched contributions
* Full training to learn the business and enhance professional skills
* Employee discounts, including discounted prices on the purchase of Avis/Budget cars
* Access to an Employee Assistance Program for services including counseling, financial and legal consultation, referrals for care service and more

**What We're Looking For:**

  

* Strong analytical and problem-solving skills — comfortable digging into data to find the "why"
* Working knowledge of P&L structure and financial analysis fundamentals
* Clear written and verbal communication skills; able to work cross-functionally
* Proficiency in Microsoft Excel; comfort with the broader Microsoft Office suite
* SQL/Python proficiency a strong plus
* Familiarity with applying AI/automation tools to reporting and analysis workflows is a plus
* A genuine curiosity and enthusiasm for the business, not just the numbers
* Bachelor’s degree in finance, accounting, economics, or related field (or equivalent experience)

The annual starting salary for this position is between $65,000 – $80,000 annually. Factors that may affect starting pay within this range include geography/market, skills, education, experience, and other qualifications of the successful candidate.

**Who We Are:**

Here at Avis Budget Group, you will be joining a team of 25,000 driven people, performing with purpose. Together, we’re moving the future of transportation forward with our innovative, customer-focused solutions.

Our culture is performance driven, where we encourage and support each other to be at our best through leadership, training, tools, and rewards.

We are proud to make a positive difference to the lives of our colleagues, customers, and communities where we operate.

*Avis Budget Group is an Equal Opportunity Employer – Qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to their race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability, status as a protected veteran or any other category protected by applicable law.*

This advertisement does not constitute a promise or guarantee of employment. This advertisement describes the general nature and level of this position only. Essential functions and responsibilities may change as business needs require. The compensation and benefits information is accurate as of the date of this posting. The Company reserves the right to modify this information at any time, with or without notice, subject to applicable law. This position may be with any affiliate of Avis Budget Group.

At Eastpak and JanSport, we are two unique brands that embody the same spirit of self-expression and discovery. Our packs reflect us as people – rugged, ready, and inspired. We’re built to resist whatever life throws at us, to express ourselves as individuals, and inspire positive resistance.

title: Finance Manager
description:
### **Description**

ELEMIS are looking for a Finance Manager to support the growth of our US business. Reporting to the Associate Director of Finance, the Finance Manager will play an integral role in supporting financial planning and performance management for the US business, acting as a key finance partner to US leadership and the Sales, Marketing and Operations teams. This role will offer strategic insight and value through advice, guidance, and recommendations for improving P&L performance.
  
  
This role will play a large part in budgeting and reforecasting, month end close activities and monitoring/controlling channel sales. The Finance Manager will also oversee spend governance, recurring management reporting, and analysis of emerging cost pressures and business opportunities.

### **What You Will Do:**

**Financial Planning & Analysis and Reporting:**

* Monthly P&L preparation and analysis; providing clear explanation of monthly, quarterly, and annual variances to senior management.
* Annual budget and periodic reforecast processes, partnering with stakeholders across the business and delivering submissions to Global Finance.
* Own US revenue forecasting, consolidating inputs across all channels and teams to maintain an accurate, up-to-date view of performance.
* Partner with Accounting and US Commercial teams on month-end close activities.
* Work closely with Sales and Marketing teams to support financial review processes including weekly, monthly, and quarterly business financial planning, forecasting, and ad hoc analysis.
* Design and develop financial models and presentations for strategic discussions with divisional heads and senior management.

**Business Intelligence:**

* Collaborate cross-functionally to support channel and division leads to ensure positive, strategic decision making, utilizing pertinent data and insights.
* Assess every aspect of the firm’s business growth plans, including revenues, expenses, and forward planning.
* Oversee spend governance and approval processes across US teams, ensuring investment is aligned to budget and business priorities.
* Monitor and analyze cost pressures and unplanned expenses assessing P&L impact and recommending actions.
* Facilitate and guide financial review meetings with business partners, Finance, and Marketing stakeholders to support strategic decision making.
* Collaborate with the team to develop enhanced analytics and drive continuous improvement in finance processes and reporting.
* Improve/increase AI usage/automation within the business.
* Additional tasks as assigned.

**Sustainability Responsibility:**

* Ensure all duties carried out and actions completed in every aspect of your role, contribute to the short and long-term Sustainability Goals set-forth by the ELEMIS - Climate, Biodiversity & People Pillars

### **What We Are Looking For:**

  

* Bachelor’s degree in accounting/finance/business administration
* FP&A or commercial finance experience, preferably in the consumer goods industry.
* Experience **owning a regional or business unit P&L** and leading **budget and reforecast cycles.**
* Expert in **financial modelling**: Advanced Microsoft Excel and PowerPoint skills for executive-level presentations; experience with ERP, planning/BI tools. Experience with utilizing AI tools a plus.
* **Executive presence**, with the ability to communicate complex financial information clearly and confidently to senior leadership.
* **Stakeholder management**: ability to influence and constructively challenge cross-functional stakeholders to help arrive at the best decision making for ELEMIS.
* **Prioritisation skills:** able to manage multiple recurring deliverables and deadlines with a high degree of autonomy.
* Strong **analytical skills**, attention to detail, and commitment to data accuracy.
* Exceptional **collaboration and communication skills**; ability to work effectively across diverse departments.
* Comfortable **dealing with ambiguity**, can navigate the complexities of a matrix environment and globally scaling organisation.

### **What We Offer You!**

  

* This is a Hybrid role based three days per week (Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday) in our NYC office, and two days (Monday and Friday) working from home
* Paid Time Off
* 401(K) with 100% match on the first 5%
* Company Holidays
* Paid Parental Leave
* Generous ELEMIS product discount
* Supplemental & Basic Life Insurance
* Dental & Vision
* Commuter benefits
* …and more perks designed around wellbeing and balance

### **About ELEMIS**

**Our People Commitments**

Justice, Equity, Diversity and Inclusion are central to our People Strategy. We are committed to building a fair, inclusive and respectful workplace where everyone feels they belong and can thrive.

We embed this commitment through inclusive hiring and progression practices, clear policies that promote equity and zero tolerance for discrimination and regular review of our people data to identify and address gaps in representation and experience. We invest in inclusive leadership, equipping our managers with the skills and accountability to foster psychologically safe, respectful and high-performing teams.

We provide channels for open dialogue, including confidential Speak Up mechanisms, to ensure concerns can be raised safely and addressed appropriately. Through ongoing learning, inclusive behaviours and shared accountability across all levels of the organisation, we empower our people to be themselves, innovate and fulfil their potential. Together, we belong.

title: Director of Technical Accounting
description:
### **Description**

The Director, Technical Accounting leads Shield’s technical accounting function and owns U.S. GAAP positions and policy across the company. This is a hands-on role as a Shield finance leader in an acquisition-driven environment: you will lead acquisition accounting from diligence through the opening balance sheet, serve as the technical resource and educator for our controllers, portfolio accounting teams, and business partners, and build the policies, playbooks, and team that let Shield’s accounting scale with the deal pipeline.
  
  
This role is hybrid, with a minimum of 3 days per week in our NYC office, plus quarterly travel for all-hands and other meetings (not expected to exceed 10%).

  

### **Key Responsibilities**

**Technical Accounting and Policy**

* Own technical accounting for business combinations (ASC 805), revenue recognition (ASC 606), including new revenue streams, leases (ASC 842), including embedded leases, and debt, equity, and deferred financing costs.

  

* Research complex arrangements and document conclusions in clear, well-reasoned technical memos; bring recommendations to Finance leadership, not just issues.

  

* Own Shield’s accounting policy framework (policy owners, review cycles, priority policies) and drive consistent adoption across portfolio companies, including capitalized software, inventory, and deferred revenue.

  

* Own the consolidated cash flow statement and supporting commentary.

  

* Partner with M&A and FP&A on earnouts so deal terms, tracking, and contingent consideration accounting stay aligned.

**Acquisition Accounting and Diligence**

* Support financial and operational due diligence on prospective acquisitions.

  

* Lead acquisition accounting, including purchase price allocations and opening balance sheets; manage third-party valuation and PPA providers.

  

* Build and maintain the PPA playbook, acquisition-terms repository, and opening balance sheet process.

  

* Partner with the Integrations team so opening balance sheets and accounting conclusions hand off cleanly to portfolio accounting teams.

**Close, Audit, and Controls**

* Review technical entries and schedules (debt, leases, revenue, equity) and deliver technical close items on the close calendar, supporting a 10-business-day close.

  

* Own technical memos and audit deliverables for technical areas; lead technical discussions with external auditors.

  

* Maintain and strengthen internal controls and SOPs over technical areas, and support control gap and material weakness remediation.

**Team Leadership and Stakeholder Education**

* Build, lead, and develop a high-performing technical accounting team, including hiring, performance management, and career development.

  

* Serve as the technical resource for Portfolio Controllers, Accounting Managers, and Senior Accountants.

  

* Lead ongoing stakeholder education across Accounting, FP&A, Integrations, Corporate Development, and portfolio company leadership, through training, playbooks, and day-to-day guidance, so complex matters are identified and escalated early.

  

* Find and implement process improvements, including automation and AI tools for schedules, memo templates, and research.

  

* Own quarterly initiatives set with Finance leadership and drive them to completion.

### **Skills, Knowledge & Expertise**

* CPA required.

  

* 10+ years of progressive accounting experience, including Big 4 or national-firm audit and technical accounting leadership in industry.

  

* Operational accounting experience in industry (close, reconciliations, controllership), so your technical conclusions work in practice, not just on paper.

  

* Deep, hands-on expertise in ASC 805, ASC 606, ASC 842, and debt and equity accounting, including purchase price allocations and contingent consideration.

  

* Experience with M&A accounting at a serial acquirer, PE-backed platform, or roll-up strongly preferred.

  

* 3+ years managing and developing accountants, with a track record of building process and documentation from the ground up.

  

* A track record of educating stakeholders: you have trained accounting teams and non-accountants on complex standards and policy, and you write audit-ready memos that people outside accounting can follow.

  

* Experience leading external audit work for technical areas; SOX or internal controls experience a plus.

  

* Proficiency with NetSuite, FloQast, Excel, and technical research tools (FASB Codification); comfort using AI tools to work faster.

  

* You take ownership, bring a recommended answer rather than just the issue, escalate judgment calls early, and hit committed dates in a fast-moving environment.

### **Job Benefits**

Base salary range of $180,000 - $210,000 / year, plus a 20% target annual bonus. Beginning 1/1/27, Shield pays 100% of the employee share of health insurance premiums, worth up to $17,000+ a year in take-home pay, along with additional benefits. Final base salary depends on experience, skills, and qualifications.

  

### **About Shield**

Shield Technology Partners is a national IT Services platform formed through the collaboration between Thrive Holdings and ZBS Partners. By combining Thrive Holdings’ technological expertise with ZBS Partners’ proven approach to supporting founder-led businesses, Shield Technology Partners is dedicated to accelerating growth, innovation and long-term value creation for IT services companies across the country.

The Financial Planning & Analysis Principal will own the financial planning and performance management engine for Delta's Media Network—including P&L management, revenue and expense forecasting, scenario and sensitivity analysis, and recurring financial reporting. This role will develop a deep understanding of every driver of the business, connecting media-specific revenue assumptions such as inventory, impressions, pricing, sell-through, and revenue share structures with the full cost base required to operate and scale the Media Network. Working closely with Media Network leadership and Delta Finance, this person will provide weekly and monthly visibility into financial performance, explain what is driving results, continuously refine the outlook, and model the financial implications of strategic and commercial decisions.

  

PRIMARY FUNCTIONS:

* P&L Management & Financial Performance: Maintain a comprehensive view of Delta’s Media Network P&L, developing a deep understanding of revenue, expenses, margins, and the underlying drivers of financial performance. Monitor actuals against plan and forecast, identify variances, and provide leadership with clear insight into what is driving results.
* Forecasting & Financial Planning: Own the development and ongoing refinement of revenue, expense, and profitability forecasts across the Media Network. Build driver-based forecasts that reflect evolving assumptions around advertiser demand, inventory, pricing, sell-through, product launches, headcount, technology, vendors, and other business drivers.
* Scenario & Sensitivity Analysis: Develop flexible financial models that allow leadership to rapidly evaluate the impact of changing business assumptions and strategic choices, including pricing, inventory growth, sell-through, channel mix, launch timing, revenue-share structures, operating models, and investment decisions.
* Media Economics & Revenue Analytics: Develop a detailed understanding of the Media Network’s revenue model and analyze performance across products, channels, advertisers, and other relevant dimensions. Connect media-specific drivers—including available inventory, impressions, CPMs, sell-through, realized pricing, and product mix—to revenue and profitability.
* Cost & Profitability Analytics: Maintain a detailed understanding of the Media Network’s cost base, including headcount, technology, data and measurement, agencies, vendors, revenue shares, and other operating expenses. Analyze cost-to-serve, contribution economics, and profitability across products, channels, and operating models to identify opportunities and risks.
* Financial Reporting & Business Insights: Develop weekly, monthly, and other recurring management reporting that provides leadership with a clear view of revenue, expenses, profitability, forecast performance, and key financial drivers. Go beyond reporting results to explain why performance is changing, what it means for the outlook, and where leadership attention is needed.
* Business Cases & Investment Analysis: Build financial models and business cases for new products, channels, technology investments, partnerships, operating-model changes, and other strategic opportunities, helping leadership understand expected returns, break-even points, sensitivities, and financial tradeoffs.
* Commercial Finance & Pricing Support: Partner with Ad Sales, Ad Products, and Business Operations to evaluate pricing, packaging, deal structures, revenue shares, and other commercial decisions. Provide financial analysis that helps balance revenue growth, advertiser value, and long-term profitability.
* Annual & Long-Range Planning: Support annual budgeting and longer-range planning for the Media Network, translating business strategy and product roadmaps into financial assumptions, investment requirements, revenue expectations, and profitability outlooks.
* Enterprise Finance Partnership: Serve as the primary analytical partner between the Media Network and Delta Finance, aligning forecasts, actuals, budgets, and planning assumptions while ensuring Media Network leadership has the level of financial detail needed to manage the business.
* Financial Modeling & Reporting Infrastructure: Build and continuously improve the models, dashboards, and analytical tools needed to provide scalable, reliable visibility into financial performance and rapidly evaluate changes in business assumptions.

Org. Setting and Reporting

This position is located in the Budget and Finance Section (BFS), Executive Office (EO), Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA) in New York. OCHA is the part of the United Nations Secretariat responsible for bringing together humanitarian actors to ensure a coherent response to emergencies. OCHA also ensures there is a framework within which each actor can contribute to the overall response effort. OCHA's mission is to mobilize and coordinate effective and principled humanitarian action in partnership with national and international actors in order to alleviate human suffering in disasters and emergencies; advocate the rights of people in need; promote preparedness and prevention and facilitate sustainable solutions. This temporary job opening is being advertised for the position of Finance and Budget Officer based in New York at UNHQ. Under the overall supervision of the Executive Officer, the Finance and Budget Officer reports directly to the Chief of Budget and Finance Section (BFS), who is based in New York.

Responsibilities

Within delegated authority, the Finance & Budget Officer will be responsible for the following duties: Programme Budget: • Reviews, analyses and finalizes the preparation of the Programme Plan Budget (PPB) and its revisions on the basis of Sub Programmes submissions, taking into account recommendations and decisions of specialized intergovernmental bodies. • Provides substantive support to relevant intergovernmental and expert bodies in their review of the PPB and its revisions; secures approval from the General Assembly. • Ensure legislative mandates are accurately translated into program budgets. • Liaises accordingly with relevant sections of the UN Controller’s office. Budget preparation: • Reviews, analyses and finalizes cost estimates and budget proposals, in terms of staff and non-staff requirements from Divisions/offices at headquarters and in the field. • Provides detailed input with respect to resource requirements for budget submissions. • Reviews, analyzes and finalizes program budget/financial implications of GA resolutions in light of additional mandates. • Provides substantive support to OCHA governance bodies in their budget review and approval processes. Budget administration: • Within delegation of authority, issues allotments, authorizes sub-allotments, including redeployment of funds when necessary, ensuring appropriate expenditures. • Manages and monitors budget implementation and recommends reallocation of funds as necessary. • Monitors expenditures to ensure that they remain within authorized levels. • Administers and monitors extra-budgetary resources, including review of agreements and cost plans, ensuring compliance with regulations and rules and established policies and procedures. • Prepares budget performance submissions. • Reviews and finalizes budget performance reports, analyzing variances between approved budgets and actual expenditures. • Provides substantive support to relevant intergovernmental and expert bodies and OCHA’s Budget Steering Committee. General • Provides advice and guidance, including training, to headquarters and field staff on budgetary and financial policies and procedures, including results-based budgeting. • Participates in inter-departmental meetings and/or technical survey missions on matters related to resource requirements, programming and budgetary issues. • Keeps up-to-date on documents/reports/guidelines that have a bearing on matters related to program budgets, ensuring compliance with intergovernmental recommendations and decisions as well as with United Nations policies and procedures. • Drafts reports for intergovernmental bodies and for management on budgetary issues, and correspondence. • Undertakes research and analysis of budgetary policies and procedures, makes recommendations for changes and/or modifications. • Acts as Approving Officer in accordance with United Nations Financial Rules and Regulations. • Ensures the integrity of financial and management systems and the controls that underpin them. • Represents OCHA Executive Office in inter and intra-departmental meetings. • May plan, organize, manage and supervise the work of the Unit assigned. • Collects and analyzes data to identify trends or patterns and provide insights through graphs, charts, tables and reports using data visualization methods to enable data-driven planning, decision-making, presentation and reporting. • Performs other duties as required.

Competencies

PROFESSIONALISM: Knowledge of financial and budgetary principles and practices, budget development and financial administration of resources. Ability to develop budgetary policies, procedures and new programmes. Ability to formulate new strategies and technical approaches to budgetary matters. Shows pride in work and in achievements; demonstrates professional competence and mastery of subject matter; is conscientious and efficient in meeting commitments, observing deadlines and achieving results; is motivated by professional rather than personal concerns; shows persistence when faced with difficult problems or challenges; remains calm in stressful situations. Takes responsibility for incorporating gender perspectives and ensuring the equal participation of women and men in all areas of work. Able to analyze and interpret data in support of decision-making and convey resulting information to management. PLANNING & ORGANIZING: Develops clear goals that are consistent with agreed strategies; identifies priority activities and assignments; adjusts priorities as required; allocates appropriate amount of time and resources for completing work; foresees risks and allows for contingencies when planning; monitors and adjusts plans and actions as necessary; uses time efficiently. ACCOUNTABILITY: Takes ownership of all responsibilities and honours commitments; delivers outputs for which one has responsibility within prescribed time, cost and quality standards; operates in compliance with organizational regulations and rules; supports subordinates, provides oversight and takes responsibility for delegated assignments; takes personal responsibility for his/her own shortcomings and those of the work unit, where applicable.

Education

Advanced university degree (Master’s degree or equivalent) in business administration, finance, or related field. A first-level university degree in combination with qualifying experience may be accepted in lieu of the advanced university degree.

Job - Specific Qualification

Successful completion of both degree and non-degree programs in data analytics, business analytics or data science programs is desirable.

Work Experience

A minimum of seven years of progressively responsible experience in finance, administration, budget, business administration or related area is required. Experience in working with trust funds, programme support costs, and the regular budget within a comparable international organization is required. Experience working with financial functions of an ERP (Enterprise Resources Planning) system - such as the Umoja Business Planning and Consolidation module - is required. Experience in directly supporting senior leadership during the presentation of budget proposals to legislative bodies is desirable. Experience in a management role supervising and coordinating a team working in budget and/or finance area is desirable.

**Counterparty Risk Group**

The counterparty credit risk management function is responsible for the management and control of counterparty risk at US Bank. Responsible for conducting pre-trade counterparty credit risk analysis for a broad range of products, including **interest rate derivatives, foreign exchange (FX) derivatives, commodity derivatives, credit derivatives, and repo transactions**. The role involves quantifying counterparty risk exposure through measures such as **Expected Exposure (EE), Potential Future Exposure (PFE), and stressed exposure metrics** to assess the potential impact of adverse market movements and counterparty default.

The analyst evaluates proposed transactions against approved credit limits, risk appetite, collateral arrangements, and regulatory requirements to ensure appropriate risk-taking and limit compliance prior to trade execution. Working closely with trading, credit, and risk management teams, the analyst identifies material risk concentrations, recommends risk mitigants where necessary, and helps ensure that counterparty credit risk is accurately measured, monitored, and controlled across the trading portfolio.

Kharon is a highly disruptive and incredibly innovative organization that navigates risk at the intersection of global security threats + international commerce.

What does that mean? Great question.

  

Operating at the nexus of global security, Kharon is on a mission to revolutionize the current landscape. We take really complex data as it relates to global security and empower our clients to not only understand the risk associated with their potential business relationships but to operationalize that data so that they can make the best and most informed decisions possible. From financial crimes and sanctions to export controls and threat identifications, our tools optimize protection against the types of risks that could otherwise be incredibly dangerous and excessively costly to any business. Serving many of today’s leading global financial and multinational institutions, Kharon products are the most powerful in the space with a precision and depth that is absolutely unparalleled.

  

When you look at any major global crisis event, we’re providing intelligence that’s at the heart of those circumstances. We connect the dots in a way that’s meaningful. Now, we’re experiencing unprecedented growth. As the world continues to evolve in complexity, so too does the demand for our products.

  

With dotted-line leadership from the Director Research, the core of this position is dedicated to conducting open-source research on a variety of foreign affairs and national security issues. More specifically, you will be researching, analyzing, and interpreting data as it relates to sanctions, export controls, and criminal/illicit networks. You will be responsible for the diligent pursuit of data as it relates to ever-evolving market demand and our client inquiries. Working collaboratively with the Kharon Research team, you will contribute to the development of new datasets and update existing ones, identifying and utilizing new sources and developing subject matter expertise on the various strategic topics. Leveraging your sound analytical approach and research techniques, you will identify data typologies and conduct risk-relevant research that contributes to the health of our data intelligence and overall platform.

To the right person, this will be the perfect kind of challenge. Our mission is compelling, our product is powerful, and we’re growing at a rate that makes us unstoppable. If you’re looking to be surrounded by people who will inspire you to think and challenge you to grow then look no further. Our team is made up of some of the most visionary and uncompromising individuals you will ever encounter. We don’t take ourselves seriously but we’re serious about the work we do and there is absolutely no slowing us down.

### **RESPONSIBILITIES:**

* Update existing research while monitoring developments on sanctions issues, regulatory environments, and other national security or compliance-related matters.
* Identify and utilize new data and sources of information to develop subject matter expertise on strategic topics related to business intelligence research, conflict and illicit finance analysis, and banking sector risk management/compliance.
* Identify risk-relevant research and data typologies, demonstrating sound analytical approaches and research techniques.
* Demonstrate creativity, resourcefulness, and innovation while maintaining a high ethical standard in working with colleagues and leaders.

### **QUALIFICATIONS:**

* A Bachelor's or Master's degree in International Relations, Political Science, Security Studies, Regional Studies, History, Sociology, or a related field.
* Language/Reading proficiency in one of the following languages: Russian, Arabic, Mandarin, Farsi or any other critical language.
* At least 2+ years of SQL and/or Python experience, including experience with academic or professional research, as well as the use of databases and online, open source resources, is essential.
* Understanding of global sanctions, international regulations, and compliance issues.
* High ethical standard, cultural awareness, and sensitivity to work respectfully in a diverse research environment.

To keep that momentum going, we do our very best to make sure that each and every team member is completely taken care of. We’re nothing without our people and we strive to offer a package that reflects that. As a Kharon team member, you can expect:

* Fully sponsored medical, dental, and vision

* Serve as a primary Yield partner to Sales, Planning, and Ad Operations, evaluating and approving pricing and inventory across multiple channels and buying methodologies, including Digital, Linear, Social, Audio, Print, and Programmatic.

* Collaborate with partners across Sales, Planning, Ad Operations, Marketing, Finance, Product, and Data to evaluate pricing, inventory, and product strategies that support near-term objectives and long-term growth.
* Analyze complex datasets and present clear findings, recommendations, and strategic points of view across the commercial organization, translating analytical concepts into actionable business narratives for different audiences.

* Comfort developing and presenting data-backed recommendations, including challenging existing approaches when marketplace or performance data supports a different strategy.

**Position Summary:** The Office of Teacher Recruitment and Quality (TRQ) is responsible for the recruitment of diverse and talented teachers to meet the staffing needs of New York Public Schools (NYCPS) and programs, as well as being responsible for initiatives to promote the equitable and quality distribution of teachers across all schools. The Office of Teacher Recruitment and Quality accomplishes its work through a strategic, data driven approach that focuses on the following efforts:

  

* Serve as the primary marketing agent and source of information to individuals seeking to become NYCPS teachers, to recruit a large, high quality, equitable and diverse pool of candidates.

**About the Metropolitan Museum of Art**

The Met presents over 5,000 years of art from around the world for everyone to experience and enjoy. The Museum lives in two iconic sites in New York City—The Met Fifth Avenue and The Met Cloisters. Millions of people also take part in The Met experience online.

Since its founding in 1870, The Met has always aspired to be more than a treasury of rare and beautiful objects. We are committed to fostering a collaborative and respectful work environment with a staff as diverse as the audiences we engage. Our staff members are art lovers who are passionate about working toward a common goal: creating the most dynamic and inspiring art museum in the world.

**Respect:** Engage one another with collegiality, empathy, and kindness, always.

**Inclusivity:** Ensure that all are and feel welcome and valued.

**Collaboration:** Reach across boundaries to exchange ideas and work together toward our shared mission.

**Excellence:** Lead the cultural world in quality and expertise—and inspire curiosity and creativity.

**Integrity:** Hold ourselves to the highest moral standards, admit when we fall short, and then evolve.

**BACKGROUND AND OVERVIEW**
---------------------------

The Met is, and sees itself as, an educational institution. The Education Department ensures that the scholarship and collection of the Museum are accessible and inviting for all audiences regardless of background, ability, age, or experience. As one of the few departments to interface across the entire institution and with the public directly, Education works daily to connect, inspire, collaborate, and innovate with its colleagues within The Met in order to better connect with and inspire its local, national, and international audience beyond it.

  

As the Head of Education, you will be responsible for overseeing over 25,000 programs a year for The Met Fifth and The Met Cloisters to a diverse local and global audience. The Department is a national and international leader in museum-based education and public programming, pushing boundaries through continuous innovation and experimentation. With over 50 education staff and over 400 volunteers, you will orchestrate various programs including: high school and college internships that promote career development and diversity; an award-winning fellowship program; pre-K to grade 12 educator programs that train teachers to integrate art into curricula across disciplines; lectures and symposia that feature preeminent artists, curators, and scholars; community engagement programs and partnerships; Cloisters' specific programming, daily tours in multiple languages; and so much more. In addition to the department’s robust programming, you will oversee all departmental activities, such as personnel management, prioritization and planning, budgeting, fundraising, and more.

The Department is organized into three main programmatic divisions, with support by an Administration and Operations arm:

* Teaching and Learning;
* Public Programs and Community Engagement;
* Academic and Research Programs, including The Met’s renowned Fellowship Program.

Reporting to the Deputy Director of Audience Engagement, who oversees a departmental group responsible for the Museum’s audience-facing content, programming, and promotions, you will work closely with partners within the Audience Engagement umbrella (Digital, Marketing, Publications, Imaging, Libraries, and Live Arts) and across the organization including Curatorial, Conservation, Science, Development, Diversity and Inclusion, Government Affairs, Membership, Special Events, Visitor Experience, Communications, Finance, and more, to support Audience Engagement’s vision to connect audiences to art, ideas, and one another to make the Museum relevant, welcoming, and accessible for all.

An ambassador for The Met, the Head is responsible for building and maintaining strong relationships with local, national, and international partners in education, government, philanthropy, peer institutions, trustees and donors, and the artists’ communities that are involved in any given offering.

--------------------------------------------------

The Met seeks a visionary leader, collaborator, and fundraiser to closely partner with the Deputy Director of Audience Engagement to help realize the Museum’s mission and vision and ensure the successful implementation of education strategies across the Museum. They are a practiced and compelling advocate for public programming for the Museum to generate excitement and to attract new audiences nationally and internationally. They will drive innovation and new initiatives to connect broader audiences with The Met’s collection and their interpretation.

**PRIMARY RESPONSIBILITIES & DUTIES**
-------------------------------------

* Envision and execute a comprehensive strategy for education that uplifts the Museum’s core mission and vision, affirms The Met as a leader in the field, and broadens access to the Museum and its collections.
* Oversee, champion, and execute an innovative and cohesive suite of programs and initiatives that uplift the Museum’s commitment to learning, engagement, and access and draw on the Museum’s collections, exhibitions, scholarship, and assets.
* Attract, lead, and motivate a diverse team of staff, interns, fellows, and vendors. Provide professional training and opportunities for growth and advancement and promote trust and collaboration across teams.
* Develop and maintain strong relationships with donors, supporters, collectors, scholars, artists, and community partners and organizations. Fundraise, analyze, and optimize established revenue streams and identify departmental and Museum-wide opportunities for new ones.
* Expand and deepen The Met’s commitment to and engagement with local communities and partners, including other educational, philanthropic, and cultural institutions, as well as partnerships with public school systems across New York State including New York City’s – as the nation’s largest and most complex.
* Drive experimentation in developing and enhancing programs and learning experiences that actively encourage new and diverse audiences to explore art and the Museum, locally and globally.
* Oversee and direct budgets, staffing, deadlines, deliverables, and competing agendas. Organize, set priorities, create action plans, delegate, coordinate, and deliver results while navigating a hierarchical complex multisite organization, establish cross-functional relationships, and build consensus.
* Other related duties as assigned.

**REQUIREMENTS & QUALIFICATIONS**
---------------------------------

* Advanced degree in education or art history preferred.
* 15 years experience of management in a museum or cultural institution. Adept at building and managing a high-performing staff and facilitating their ability to work collaboratively and deliver results as a team.
* 10 years demonstrated experience in articulating and driving a distinctive organizational, cultural, or educational vision and mobilizing internal and external support for programs to realize new levels of success.

ISS STOXX is Hiring in our New York office! We seek an Index Associate to join the Index Surveillance & Monitoring team within Index Operations Department.

The successful candidate will join a dynamic global team responsible for the accuracy, integrity, and dissemination of STOXX and DAX Indices.

In this role, you will support the configuration, calculation, monitoring, and dissemination of indices, including real-time market surveillance, oversight of third-party calculation agents, and a range of index operations and governance activities.

You will also contribute to strategic initiatives, including new index integrations, process enhancements, and automation projects in partnership with IT, while supporting both day-to-day operations and broader business objectives.

### **Key Responsibilities**

* Monitor real-time market data used in index calculations and ensure the accuracy and integrity of index values.
* Perform surveillance of index calculation processes and investigate potential issues or exceptions.
* Oversee and coordinate with third-party calculation agents.
* Support ownership research activities and provide timely, accurate information to clients through publications and notifications.
* Contribute to the integration of new index concepts into existing monitoring and surveillance frameworks.
* Partner with IT and other stakeholders to identify and implement automation and process improvement opportunities.
* Participate in both day-to-day operational activities and longer-term strategic projects.
* Collaborate with colleagues across global locations to support a consistent and high-quality index management framework.

* Master's degree in Finance, Economics, Mathematics, or a related field preferred.
* 1-2+ years of experience in a financial markets environment, preferably within the index industry, asset management, portfolio management, product development, structuring, or related financial services fields.
* Strong understanding of financial markets, market data, and the principles governing index and portfolio valuation.
* Knowledge of corporate actions and their impact on index calculation methodologies.
* Experience with fixed income portfolio management and valuation is preferred.
* Experience in corporate actions management, index operations, securities operations, listed company operations, data analysis, data cleansing, or data processing techniques is a plus.
* Strong analytical and conceptual skills with the ability to identify issues, evaluate solutions, and manage competing priorities.
* Ability to work effectively under pressure, handle multiple tasks simultaneously, and meet tight deadlines.
* Self-starter who can work and learn independently with minimal supervision.

* Familiarity with market data platforms such as Bloomberg and Refinitiv.
* Python, VBA, SQL, or database knowledge is beneficial but not required.
* Strong attention to detail with the ability to quickly identify, investigate, and escalate issues when appropriate.
* Excellent communication skills and a collaborative approach to working across teams and functions.
* Flexible, highly motivated, solution-oriented, and committed to delivering high-quality work in a fast-paced environment.

This role offers the opportunity to work on both operational and strategic initiatives within a growing area of the business while contributing to the continued development and oversight of some of the industry's leading index solutions.

title: CHIEF OF BRANCH (Chief, Policy and Programming Branch), D1
description:
Org. Setting and Reporting

In its resolution A/RES/72/279, the United Nations General Assembly endorsed the transformation of the Development Coordination Office (DCO) into a stand-alone coordination office within the United Nations Secretariat. DCO exercises managerial and oversight functions over the Resident Coordinator system, under the collective ownership of the members of the United Nations Sustainable Development Group (UNSDG). The position is located in the DCO Headquarters in New York and reports to the Assistant Secretary-General for Development Coordination.

Responsibilities

The Chief, Policy and Programming Branch leads, guides and formulates the substantive work of the Branch. The Chief oversees the management of activities undertaken within the Branch and ensures that programmed activities are carried out in a timely fashion and co-ordinates policy, programming, data and digital work across the Resident Coordinator system. The Chief provides strategic vision, leadership, and oversight to the Branch, which includes: a) the Development Programme Cycle Section, b) the Complex Settings Section, c) the SDG Policy and Financing Section, d) the Data, Digital and Innovation Section. Within the limits of delegated authority, the incumbent is responsible for the following: • Supervises the work of the Policy and Programming Branch, • Provides overall leadership and guidance to ensure a coherent and integrated support package to Resident Coordinators (RCs), Resident Coordinator Offices (RCOs) and United Nations Country Teams (UNCTs) on sustainable development policy and implementation. • Provides strategic advice to DCO senior management on norm-based integrated sustainable development policy and implementation support matters. • Forges and maintains strategic partnerships with other entities of the United Nations Development System (UNDS), including through UNSDG mechanisms, and external partners with a view to ensuring the provision of strong system-wide support and cutting-edge expertise to RCs, RCOs and UNCTs on sustainable development policy, financing and implementation support matters. • Drives thought leadership within DCO and the UNSDG on sustainable development Policy and implementation support matters based on an effective policy-practice feedback loop that informs both Headquarters and field on these issues, while driving innovation and change in the operational support of the UNDS to the 2030 Agenda. • Leads the development of strategic, flagship sustainable development policy and implementation support products for presentation to intergovernmental bodies such as the Economic and Social Council, the General Assembly and other policy-making organs. • Reports to intergovernmental bodies on on programmatic/ substantive issues, particularly those presented in biannual and/or annual reports. • Leads the RC system’s digital transformation, including strategic oversight of digital public goods, AI-informed processes, data platforms (e.g., UN Info), and advanced analytics and innovation. • Ensures that RCs and UNCTs benefit from fit-for-purpose digital and data solutions, fostering a culture of continuous learning, experimentation and innovation across the system. • Ensures that all outputs produced by the Sections under his/her supervision meet required standards before completion to ensure they comply with the relevant mandates. • Assists the DCO Senior Management in preparing the work programme of the Department, determining priorities, and allocating resources for the completion of outputs and their timely delivery. • Undertakes or oversees the tasks necessary for the functioning of Branch including preparation of budgets, reporting on budget/programme performance, evaluation of staff performance, interviews of candidates for job openings, evaluation of candidates and preparation of inputs for results-based budgeting. • Oversees the RC system’s efforts to implement UN system-wide action plans on gender equality, disability inclusion and youth. • Oversees staff recruitment, taking due account of geographical balance. • Manages, guides, develops and trains staff under his/her supervision. • Fosters teamwork and communication among staff in the Branch and across organizational boundaries. • Oversees the organization of meetings, seminars, etc. on substantive issues. Manages the substantive preparation and organization of such meetings or seminars. • Participates in international, regional or national meetings and provides programmatic/substantive expertise on relevant issues, and holds programmatic/substantive and organizational discussions with representatives of other organizations/strategic partners. • Fosters cross-DCO teamwork, shared accountability, and a UN 2.0 leadership mindset across teams. • Represents the Branch and DCO at international, regional or national meetings.

Competencies

PROFESSIONALISM: Knowledge of the substantive field of work in general and of specific areas being supervised. Ability to produce reports and papers on technical issues and to review and edit the work of others. Ability to apply UN rules, regulations, policies and guidelines in work situations. Shows pride in work and in achievements; demonstrates professional competence and mastery of subject matter; is conscientious and efficient in meeting commitments, observing deadlines and achieving results; is motivated by professional rather than personal concerns; shows persistence when faced with difficult problems or challenges; remains calm in stressful situations. CREATIVITY: Promotes stakeholder-centered design and appropriate risk-taking approaches for team. Leads in the identification of innovative solutions to facilitate and support scaling of UNDS innovations at country level. Actively seeks to improve programmes or services; offers new and different options to solve problems or meet client needs; promotes and persuades others to consider new ideas; takes calculated risks on new and unusual ideas; thinks “outside the box”; takes an interest in new ideas and new ways of doing things; is not bound by current thinking or traditional approaches. CLIENT ORIENTATION: Considers all those to whom services are provided to be “clients” and seeks to see things from clients’ point of view; establishes and maintains productive partnerships with clients by gaining their trust and respect; identifies clients’ needs and matches them to appropriate solutions; monitors ongoing developments inside and outside the clients’ environment to keep informed and anticipate problems; keeps clients informed of progress or setbacks in projects; meets timeline for delivery of products or services to client. Managerial Competencies VISION: Identifies strategic issues, opportunities and risks; clearly communicates links between the Organization’s strategy and the work unit’s goals; generates and communicates broad and compelling organizational direction, inspiring others to pursue that same direction; conveys enthusiasm about future possibilities. JUDGEMENT/DECISION-MAKING: Identifies the key issues in a complex situation, and comes to the heart of the problem quickly; gathers relevant information before making a decision; considers positive and negative impacts of decisions prior to making them; takes decisions with an eye to the impact on others and on the Organization; proposes a course of action or makes a recommendation based on all available information; checks assumptions against facts; determines that the actions proposed will satisfy the expressed and underlying needs for the decision; makes tough decisions when necessary.

Education

Advanced university degree (Master’s degree or equivalent) in business or public administration, finance, accounting, law, social sciences or related area. A first-level university degree in combination with qualifying experience may be accepted in lieu of the advanced university degree.

description:

--------------------------------

Working at Citi is far more than just a job. A career with us means joining a team of approximately 219,000 dedicated people from around the globe. At Citi, you’ll have the opportunity to grow your career, give back to your community and make a real impact.

**Job Overview**
----------------

**You are the brain behind our work …**

At Citi, we do not just adapt to change – we drive it. Our Summer Technology Analyst Program is where forward thinking talents meet unparalleled opportunities. This is your chance to innovate, influence, and make an impact in the most global financial institution!

Citi Technology partners to ensure that Citi’s platforms can “Be the Best” for clients globally, with a diverse and ethical workforce that applies innovation and automation to deliver a world class client experience and strengthen our reputation. We have over 30,000 technologists globally who are dedicated to serving our clients’ needs across the firm. By utilizing a broad range of technologies, we are at the forefront of innovation. We seek to drive our systems and processes towards scalable, low-latency, high-performance enterprise systems to support Citi’s strategic priorities.

Summer Analysts often return to Citi after graduating from university to become Full-Time Analysts and continue their career in technology.

**Your time here will look like this...**

You will work in an agile software development environment, developing quality and scalable software solutions using leading-edge technologies. Based on business requirements, you will develop code consistent with quality standards and offer support during testing cycles and post-production deployment. To ensure defect-free programming, you will use the appropriate tools to test and debug code and participate in the review of peer coding. You have additional support, too. You join a cohort of other new hires and go through training together to learn about our company, our tools and processes, and the technical skills you will need to succeed.

* **Back-End Development:** Java, Python, Spring Framework

* **Front-End Development:** Web (React, TypeScript, Angular, HTML5) and Mobile (Swift, Kotlin)

* **Generative AI & AI Agents****:** GitHub Copilot with various models, Citi Squad (automated code reviews), Devin.AI (Agentic Code generation), Prompt Engineering, Workflow Design, GenAI Optimization, Stylus Workspaces (In-house Gemini)

* **Global Exposure**: Work in globally scoped projects with cross-functional teams and gain insights into how technology drives the financial sector worldwide.

* Graduation between Dec 2027 and May 2028.
* Educational background: Bachelor's degree in computer science, Computer Engineering, Information Technology, Management Information Systems, or other tech related degrees.
* GPA of 3.0 or better is preferred.
* A proactive problem-solver who thrives on innovation and embraces challenges with enthusiasm, leveraging Generative AI to address complex business problems and create novel solutions.
* Possess a global outlook and willingness to collaborate across cultures and time zones.
* Have excellent communication skills, project management, leadership, attention to detail, and the ability to work well within diverse teams.
* Ability to pass technical interviews consisting of basic algorithmic programming exercises.
* Must be collaborative and adaptable, with excellent communication skills. Prior experience working in agile teams is desirable.
* Work Authorization: Authorized to work in US without the need for employer sponsorship, now or in the future.

**Who we think will be a great fit...**

A steadfast dedication to learning and a true passion for business are vital. As global industries continue to evolve, we are seeking professionals who bring a global perspective to the future of banking and are eager to make an impact at the corporate level using AI. We value diversity and so do you.

This program is ideal for those who:

* Are ambitious, with a relentless drive to succeed in a fast-paced, dynamic environment.
* Are curious about how technology can revolutionize finance and are eager to be at the forefront of this transformation.

For over 25 years, Global Relay has set the standard in enterprise information archiving with industry-leading cloud archiving, surveillance, eDiscovery, and analytics solutions. We believe great businesses thrive on diversity, inclusion, and the contributions of all employees. To that end, we recruit candidates from different backgrounds and foster a work environment that encourages employees to collaborate and learn from each other, completely free of barriers.

**Your Role**

As Senior Manager, Customer Success Operations, you will lead the operational processes, insights and frameworks that enable our global Customer Success organisation to deliver customer value, protect recurring revenue and scale effectively.

Supporting approximately 50 Customer Success professionals, you will partner closely with the Chief Customer Officer and Global Head of Sales Operations to strengthen customer engagement, renewals and account growth. You will translate business priorities into practical processes, reliable reporting and clear accountability across the post-sales customer lifecycle.

This is a hands-on leadership role combining strategic planning with operational delivery. You will lead a geographically distributed team and partner with Customer Success, Sales, Finance and Product to support an increasingly complex enterprise customer base.

**Renewal Strategy and Revenue Protection**

* Build a proactive renewal operating model with clear milestones, ownership and escalation routes ahead of contract expiry.
* Support the transition from reactive auto-renewals to planned, strategic renewal discussions, including multi-year agreements where appropriate.
* Establish visibility into upcoming renewals, customer risk, contraction and expansion opportunities.
* Partner with Customer Success and Finance to improve renewal forecasting and explain revenue movements.

* Own the operational coordination of contract reconciliations and true-ups, partnering with Finance and account owners to ensure accurate, timely billing.

* Establish effective working practices across New York, London and Vancouver.

title: Program Manager, Partnerships
description:
At Braze, we have found our people. We're a genuinely approachable, exceptionally kind, and intensely passionate crew.

We seek to ignite that passion by setting high standards, championing teamwork, and creating work-life harmony as we collectively navigate rapid growth on a global scale while striving for greater equity and opportunity – inside and outside our organization.

To flourish here, you must be prepared to set a high bar for yourself and those around you. There is always a way to contribute: Acting with autonomy, having accountability and being open to new perspectives are essential to our continued success.

Our deep curiosity to learn and our eagerness to share diverse passions with others gives us balance and injects a one-of-a-kind vibrancy into our culture.

If you are driven to solve exhilarating challenges and have a bias toward action in the face of change, you will be empowered to make a real impact here, with a sharp and passionate team at your back. If Braze sounds like a place where you can thrive, we can't wait to meet you.

#### **The Role**

The Partnerships department operates in a fast-paced environment with a lean team. Key priorities arise from major events like SKO or Forge Partner Day, cross-functional initiatives, and urgent executive inquiries. Top-tier partnership teams require a dedicated program manager to own these priorities, drive execution, and maintain clear visibility into project status, blockers, and ownership.

Operating across the entire department rather than within a single partner segment, this role collaborates across every functional pillar. Key responsibilities centre on establishing clear workstream visibility and managing high-priority ad-hoc projects. This includes maintaining an accurate single source of truth for ongoing department initiatives, supporting program management for flagship events such as SKO, Forge Partner Day, and the departmental kick-off, and partnering closely with the AVP, Partner Experience to maintain the departmental operating rhythm—encompassing OKRs, business reviews, strategic narratives, All Hands meetings, and internal communications.

Rapid growth has outpaced formal tracking, leaving initiatives reliant on informal ownership and tracking. We need a program manager to establish structure, seamlessly manage diverse workstreams, and build lasting, repeatable processes. Success is defined by delivering high-quality projects on time and maintaining clear, transparent visibility into overall department status.

#### **What You'll Own**

* **Workstream visibility.** Maintain one view of cross-departmental initiatives: owners, status, dependencies and risks, with Jira as the source of truth. Run regular check-ins that keep it honest, raise concerns before they become surprises, and give leadership a clear picture of what is moving and what is not.
* **Ad-hoc and flagship projects.** Take projects from brief to delivery: agree scope and owners, build the plan, chase the dependencies, manage the timeline and run the follow-up.
* **Company moments such as SKO and Forge Partner Day.** Support the Partnerships contribution to events where the department is on stage. This may include working with leadership on the narrative and theme, briefing speakers, gathering content from pillar leads and coordinating with Marketing and Events.
* **Cross-functional initiatives.** Drive initiatives that cut across teams and need a single owner for delivery, such as moving a process from one team to another or launching a change that touches several pillars. Clarify who does what, keep the work moving and close it out properly.
* **Operating rhythm.** Support the department's OKRs, monthly and quarterly business reviews, quarterly narratives and monthly All Hands. Build the trackers and templates, chase inputs, prepare pre-reads and help run the sessions, so that leaders spend their time on decisions.
* **Communications and PR-FAQs.** Support the cadence of department updates and the PR-FAQ tracker for major launches, so that format, tone and timing stay consistent and status is honest.
* **Planning and engagement.** Support the SVP, Partnerships and Partner Operations team with annual planning, and the follow-up from the employee engagement survey in Culture Amp: tracking actions through to completion and reporting back on what changed.
* **Salesforce alignment.** If the acquisition of Braze by Salesforce completes, help plan and track the work to bring the Braze partner program in line with the broader Salesforce partner program and ecosystem, and keep it visible alongside everything else in flight.

#### **What This Role Is Really About**

A department our size can't hire a specialist for every function, and shouldn't. What it needs is someone who can pick up whatever matters most this month, run it properly and leave something behind that works without them. One month that is the narrative and run of show for Forge Partner Day. The next it is an initiative that three teams each assume another team owns. The through-line is visibility: whatever you are working on, people can see where it stands.

You will not own the content or the decisions. Pillar leads own their numbers and their stories, and leadership owns the choices. You own the delivery and the clarity around it. That means asking the question that exposes a gap in a plan, noticing when a deadline will slip a week before it does, and telling a leader that their narrative buries the lead. You do this without formal authority, and you earn trust by making everyone else's job easier.

You will also see things that are sensitive: survey results, plans in progress, changes to the organisation. Discretion is part of the job.

#### **How We Show Up**

* **Drives ownership to completion.** You step in to claim unassigned initiatives, assign clear accountability, and steer them through to successful execution.
* **Communicates with clarity and impact.** You distill complex updates into concise, actionable briefs for leadership and facilitate decisive, productive meetings.
* **Ensures end-to-end transparency.** You maintain clear and dependable tracking of progress, status, and risks, flagging delays early alongside practical solutions.
* **Leads through influence and trust.** You motivate senior leaders to hit deadlines by making collaboration seamless and consistently delivering value.
* **Balances strategy with tactical detail.** You seamlessly transition from managing detailed operational schedules to briefing executives on complex cross-functional dependencies.
* **Upholds strict confidentiality.** You handle sensitive and unreleased information with complete discretion and earn executive trust.

#### **Who You Are**

* 5-8 years in program management, project management or strategy and operations roles at a B2B SaaS or technology company, ideally supporting a go-to-market, partnerships or alliances team
* Has driven cross-functional programs from brief to delivery with several stakeholders and senior people, and has run events or company moments with speakers, content and a tight timeline
* Has built visibility across a portfolio of workstreams, using trackers, status reporting and tools such as Jira, and knows how to keep them honest without making them a burden
* A strong writer and storyteller, able to turn updates and numbers into something leaders grasp quickly
* Skilled at facilitation: you run meetings with senior people, keep them to time, and leave with clear actions and owners
* Data-driven, comfortable building trackers and spotting when numbers don't add up
* Highly organised, able to manage many deadlines and very different kinds of work at once without losing detail
* Happy to build process from nothing, and pragmatic about keeping it light enough to survive a busy quarter

description:

If you are highly motivated, adaptable and energized by fast-moving technology, Hazen may be the place for you.

This position, which reports directly to the Director of Information Technology, leads the day-to-day support, adoption and governance of the firm’s AI tools: enterprise assistants like Copilot and Claude, AI features inside engineering and design software, and internal automations. Serves as the link between IT, project teams and leadership, so that staff use AI tools productively, safely and within firm policy.

This position will partner closely with senior members of the IT team and Design Technology, building on existing workflows and system requirements to shape how AI is supported across the firm. Candidates must work well in a team environment, be able to effectively prioritize and execute tasks, and be willing to learn and develop new skills that support the responsibilities outlined below. Because AI tools and the way Hazen uses them are changing quickly, the right person is nimble and responsive: able to reprioritize quickly, resolve issues as they arise, and adapt the support model as new tools and needs emerge.

Within the first year, AI is part of how nearly everyone at Hazen works. Staff in every office and practice group use approved AI tools confidently, productively and safely, and the support, training and governance model keeps pace as the tools evolve.

**Why Hazen and Sawyer:**

* Founded in 1951 by the son of Allen Hazen (developer of the Hazen-Williams equation), we are an employee-owned company with a singular focus on "all things water."
* Our work includes planning, design, and oversight of construction of environmental infrastructure – for water, wastewater, and stormwater management.
* We foster a work environment low on bureaucracy and high in creativity.
* We recruit talented professionals, provide them with challenging, interesting, and creative assignments, and furnish them with the tools they need to succeed.
* We currently have over 2,000 employees in 70+ offices throughout the United States, Latin America, Canada, and the UK.
* A flexible hybrid work schedule supports today's busy professionals.

**Key Responsibilities will include, but not be limited to:**

* Own the support model for enterprise AI tools: intake, triage, escalation paths, knowledge base and service levels, in coordination with the Helpdesk Manager.
* Administer AI platforms: licensing, user provisioning, connectors and integrations, usage monitoring and cost tracking.
* Approve AI tools, pilots, integrations and configuration changes within firm policy, with the authority to act quickly and escalate to the Director of Information Technology only when risk, cost or a policy exception requires it.
* Run adoption and training: onboarding sessions, prompt libraries, office hours and a champions network across offices and practice groups.
* Partner with Design Technology on AI in engineering workflows (BIM/CAD, GIS, modeling, document production) and on evaluating new tools.
* Monitor new AI tools and features, including Copilot, Claude and AI in engineering software, assess their impact and opportunity, and adapt the support model and guidance as the technology evolves.
* Administer and uphold AI governance in partnership with the Director of Information Technology: the firm’s AI acceptable-use policy and its ongoing refinement, data classification (client confidentiality, CUI/ITAR where it applies), vendor security reviews, and records retention for AI outputs.
* Collect use cases from the business, prioritize them, and pilot automations or agents that deliver clear, practical value to project teams and the business.
* Report to IT leadership on how AI tools are being used, what is working, and where risks and opportunities exist.
* Supervise or mentor AI support analysts and coordinate with external vendors.
* Occasional travel may be required.

**Required Qualifications:**

* Bachelor’s degree in IT, Computer Science, Engineering or related field, or equivalent experience.
* 7+ years in IT support, systems administration or digital enablement, including 3+ years leading people or programs, with a record of driving technology adoption or organizational change.
* Hands-on administration of enterprise AI platforms (Copilot, Claude or similar) and M365 tools (Entra ID, Purview, SharePoint/Teams).
* Working knowledge of LLM concepts, prompt design, data privacy and AI risk frameworks such as NIST AI RMF.
* Strong training and communication skills, with the ability to explain technical limits to non-technical staff.
* Demonstrated ability to thrive in a fast-changing environment: responsive, adaptable and comfortable reprioritizing quickly as needs shift.

**Preferred Qualifications:**

* AEC or engineering industry experience.
* ITIL certification.
